claim: Orchid is the first code-generation benchmark specifically designed with ambiguous requirements, comprising 1,304 function-level tasks across four ambiguity types: lexical, syntactic, semantic, and vagueness.
stance_target: existence and scope of prior work on requirement ambiguity in code generation
quoted_support: It comprises 1,304 function-level tasks covering four distinct types of ambiguity: lexical, syntactic, semantic, and vagueness.

claim: Requirement ambiguity consistently degrades LLM code-generation performance, with the most pronounced negative effects on the most advanced models.
stance_target: ambiguous specifications causally reduce code LLM correctness
quoted_support: Our results demonstrate that ambiguity consistently degrades the performance of all evaluated LLMs, with the most pronounced negative effects observed in highly advanced models.

claim: LLMs frequently produce functionally divergent implementations for the same ambiguous requirement and lack the capability to autonomously identify or resolve the ambiguity.
quoted_support: LLMs frequently produce functionally divergent implementations for the same ambiguous requirement and lack the capability to identify or resolve such ambiguity autonomously.

claim: Orchid labels ambiguity type at the whole-task level (one label per task) and scores whole-function correctness, not sub-requirement-level ambiguity within a single multi-requirement task.
stance_target: granularity gap a per-requirement harness could exploit
quoted_support: It comprises 1,304 function-level tasks covering four distinct types of ambiguity: lexical, syntactic, semantic, and vagueness.
